title: 入口｜空と旅客機を先に見せ、「空に入る」へ。検討用画像・未実装。
prompt:
Create ONE polished landscape 16:10 review-only interface concept for the existing independent Japanese WebXR airliner sound-observation service AIRPLANEVOICE. This is a visual direction mock-up for the entrance screen, not a claim of implemented functionality. Use reference image 1 for the existing warm-ivory, deep-teal, restrained Japanese application character and quiet horizon. Use reference image 2 as the identity anchor for the aircraft: preserve its recognizable white civil four-engine passenger airliner, long clean fuselage, swept wings, dark teal vertical tail, small dark windows, four turbofan nacelles. Improve only the lighting and visual treatment, do not replace it with a fighter, business jet or another category.

Composition: ONE clean complete interface screen, not a collage, no device frame. Landscape 16:10. Immersive bright clear morning blue sky fills nearly the entire screen, subtle atmospheric depth, very low calm tree-lined horizon and pale grass only in bottom 12 percent. Large generous negative space. A single airliner at upper-right, about 20 percent of screen width, visible from ground in graceful side/underside three-quarter view, with a broad beautiful soft sunlight highlight grazing the white fuselage and wing. Elegant physical presence, unhurried stable flight. A short extremely subtle acoustic curve trails behind it; fine and low contrast, fading with age, no large circles or ripples.

Interface: thin understated header with AIRPLANEVOICE in refined deep-teal uppercase typography at upper-left and a tiny simple abstract route/plane mark. A compact warm ivory entrance panel in the lower-left, airy and well spaced, occupying about 28 percent width and 36 percent height. Japanese heading roughly expressing watching the sky and listening, with only a very small amount of readable Japanese copy, no statistics, fabricated endorsements or technical jargon. One confident deep-teal rounded-rectangle primary button labelled 空に入る. Beneath it a quiet segmented VR / AR choice and a modest speaker sound-control icon with 音. Aviation personality appears through a hairline runway-centerline motif, a fine route stroke and crisp airport-wayfinding alignment, not through a cockpit frame. Slightly translucent ivory panel, minimal border, soft natural shadow. Restrained typography, calm museum exhibit / premium airport information quality. Keep every control calm and simple; the aircraft and open sky are the emotional center.

Color palette: warm ivory #F4F3EC, deep teal #154F55, clear morning blue #9BC7DC, muted green #819789, soft warm sunlight. No saturated neon, no sci-fi HUD, no portal, no fighter-jet aggression, no gauges, no busy technical dashboard, no huge rings, no giant dramatic sun, no lens flare streak, no extra aircraft. The full screen should feel peaceful, tactile, aviation-specific and welcoming, with believable attainable web-app UI and an aspirational sunlit aircraft render.

title: 観察｜光を受ける白い旅客機と、広い空。目標とする雰囲気の案。
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / concept exploration, not an implemented product screenshot.
Create ONE clean wide landscape 16:10 first-person VR observation screen concept for AIRPLANEVOICE, based on the supplied reference screenshots. Reference 1 is current product look and Japanese interface; Reference 2 defines the aircraft silhouette and white four-engine airliner with dark teal tail. Preserve the passenger airliner identity; do not make a fighter or spacecraft. It may be refined in surface quality.
The concept direction is calm bright morning, attentive listening and looking up, natural high-end aviation museum wayfinding. A beautiful large but convincingly distant four-engine passenger airliner passes through the upper-middle-right of an expansive pale blue sky, warm sunlight makes a broad soft highlight across its white fuselage, wings have quiet dark undersides. Plane about 18-22% of image width, viewed from the ground slightly from below, realistic perspective, no dramatic banking. Low simple muted sage-green horizon and a few stylized trees retain the current app's character. No major buildings.
Most of the frame is uncluttered sky. A single extremely faint short acoustic trail curve stays BEHIND and clear of the aircraft; no bright waves over its body, no thick contrail, no full-screen particles. At the bottom, a compact refined semitransparent ivory/teal control dock occupying less than 15% of the image, legible minimal proposed Japanese labels only: 空を眺める, 現実に重ねる, 地図, 音. Small AIRPLANEVOICE wordmark, quiet volume icon, soft thin line motifs inspired by route lines/runway wayfinding. Warm ivory #f4f2e8, deep teal #173f45, muted mint #c3e5e0, tiny restrained warm brass accents.
No browser chrome, no headset border or stereo doubled view, no fake performance statistics, no AI conversation, no demo completion claims. No sci-fi cockpit HUD, neon purple, giant glass cards, horizon tilt, dark movie color grading or visible people. This is a coherent, attainable art/UI direction evolved from the current procedural application, not a new game or marketing poster. Give one polished full-screen visual, not a collage or a presentation sheet.

EDIT (second pass)
Edit this UI concept image with ONE precise change only: remove the thin pale curved line and tiny white bright speck in the sky to the LEFT of the airplane's nose, reconstructing clean matching blue sky there. That line incorrectly appears in front of this left-facing airplane; it must be absent. Preserve the entire airplane, all four engines, its size and position, the sunlight, trees, horizon, cloud textures, exact bottom UI and Japanese labels, composition and dimensions. Add nothing. This remains a proposed design image, not a product screenshot.

title: VR→AR｜背景が静かに透け、機体と音は続く。切り替え途中の構想。
prompt:
Create ONE review-only UI concept image for the independent AIRPLANEVOICE / SOUND TRAIL immersive web experience. This is an ILLUSTRATIVE FUTURE DESIGN, not an implemented screenshot and not a passthrough photograph. The lower exhibition room is an invented neutral physical-room example because the real venue is unknown. Use the two reference images to preserve the existing project's calm cream, deep teal and mint visual identity and the recognizable white four-engine passenger jet with dark teal tail. Do not copy the old desktop dashboard.

OUTPUT: one clean landscape 16:10 frame, no collage, no panels, no comparison layout, no annotations.
CAMERA: a single stationary ground-observer viewpoint, looking slightly upward. No cockpit, window frame, head-mounted frame or hands. Same scene and aircraft stay spatially anchored during the switch.
AIRCRAFT: one solid, fully opaque white four-engine passenger airliner, dark teal tail, flying toward the right, upper-middle of frame, about 20 percent of image width. Credible large passenger-jet silhouette and swept wings. Show subtle warm morning-sun reflection along the fuselage side. Keep its entire silhouette readable, with no trails or UI crossing it.
WORLD AND TRANSITION: illustrate the midpoint of a quiet 0.9-second VR-to-AR opacity reveal. Upper half remains a beautiful clear morning soft blue virtual sky. In the lower third, a modest neutral real exhibition room and one simple pale wood table emerge through an extremely softly dissolving virtual green field and low horizon. Allow faint translucent grass/landscape to be seen over parts of the table and room, as if only environmental opacity is decreasing. The aircraft stays fully visible above it. Room walls and table are clean, plausible, cream and muted neutral colors, with no brands, posters, people or legible booth information. The transition must read at first glance as a quiet gradual appearance of physical space beneath a retained airplane, not a portal, vertical hard split, dramatic sweep or giant decorative wave.
SOUND VISUAL: at most one short, very fine, pale mint acoustic arc well behind the jet on the left, separated from its silhouette. No continuous glowing runway, giant curves, rings enclosing the viewer or flashy effects.
UI: a single small unobtrusive frosted dark-teal rounded pill near bottom center with a restrained white icon and tiny Japanese label 「現実に重ねる」. This is the only text. No dashboard, sidebars or giant title.
MOOD: serene, light, unhurried, believable immersive experience; the aircraft and its sound are the main event. Refined editorial art direction. Soft natural morning lighting. Avoid neon, sci-fi, cockpit motifs, black flash, white flash, clouds covering the eyes, tunnel, camera movement, acceleration or fade-to-black.

title: 会場｜小さな地図から実寸の地点へ。架空の配置図・将来の案。
prompt:
Create exactly ONE polished visual concept screen, landscape 16:10, for a proposed AIRPLANEVOICE exhibition-map AR experience. This is a design exploration, not an actual app screenshot or actual venue capture. Use the first reference for the current restrained ivory/deep-teal/muted-mint visual identity and three-point map. Use the second reference for the recognisable white passenger airliner with dark teal tail and FOUR underwing engines. Improve visual design substantially while keeping the product calm and plausible.

First-person eye-level view from a person standing beside a small fixed light-wood table in a neutral real exhibition room. Broad warm white diffuse room lighting, ivory walls, softly out-of-focus empty demonstration booths in the distance. No people needed. The room should feel open and ordinary, not sci-fi. Keep most of the view unobstructed, with generous breathing space.

Above the table, place one elegant compact rectangular virtual floorplan board, slightly tilted toward the viewer, physically about 60 cm wide. It must remain small enough to see the real surroundings, occupying about the lower-middle third of the screen. Deep teal base, extremely subtle flat or low-relief white booth footprints and pale mint floorplan lines, thin soft edge. It is a small floorplan, NOT a fantasy miniature city, dome, hologram tower or game terrain. Show exactly three distinct easy-to-read rounded numbered booth markers: 1, 2 and 3. Marker 2 is selected with a restrained warm amber ring; the other two are muted mint. No actual exhibition booth names. Include a very thin and unobtrusive curved route hint between two points as a speculative future guide path, without a bright ribbon. No excessive labels or information.

A small white FOUR-engine passenger airliner with dark teal tail is flying above the map and into the open space of the room, as a proposed guide. Calm heavy-airliner pose with almost level wings. Front three-quarter angle makes its two engines under each wing unambiguous. Aircraft must look like an airliner, not a fighter, drone, toy or spacecraft. Soft warm highlights on fuselage and subdued reflections. Aircraft guide scale and route are conceptual rather than a current implemented feature.

At the lower edge of the map, a single compact clean floating ivory control strip with only three legible Japanese labels: 「小さな地図」 「実寸」 「空へ」. The first is subtly selected in deep teal. Typography clean and large enough to read, with clear spacing. Do not add other text, numbers, logos, title banners, performance statistics, chat, invented answers, loading messages or screenshots-within-screenshots. Optionally a tiny understated microphone pictogram at the end of the strip, indicating a future voice entry, but do not show active AI responses.

Overall: a high-quality contemporary spatial product design proposal, warm ivory + deep teal + muted mint, selected amber only, gentle shadows and exceptional restraint. Treat the aircraft as the emotional focal point; map as a useful instrument. No laser holograms, neon glow, portals, cockpit framing, intrusive HUD, sci-fi effects, split views, collage, storyboard, annotated mockup or hardware headset visible. ONE coherent landscape image.
routeName: 静かな誘導と、つながる空
